name: The detective's hands (narrator rig)
role: the unseen narrator's two steady, cuffed hands (a mid-life teacher's, never an old man's): the only part of the detective ever shown; they do most of the film's acting at the Case Board, the candle shelf, the Wall of Forecasts and the manila file
signature: two steady, cuffed tweed forearms entering from the bottom of frame on the lamp side (frame lower-right, L5), never a body, never a face; the signet ring kept; no age marks, no liver spots, no tremor (the narrator is mid-life, forties or fifties)

rig.entry: a fixed lamp-side entry point at the frame's lower right edge; forearms slide in on twos along a shallow arc and withdraw the same way
parts: right forearm + tweed cuff + shirt cuff
left forearm + tweed cuff + shirt cuff
handArt sprite per action (swapped, not morphed)
rig.rimLight: the desk lamp's warm rim on the upper edge of each cuff and knuckle; everything else ink

actions.pin: press a card or slip onto the board or Wall with a brass pin (thumb push, a small settle)
actions.unpinDrop: pinch a card off its pin and let it fall into the lamp's pool, or set it down
actions.strikeLight: strike a match on the box and light a candle wick or lantern (the only fire-making action)
actions.fileFold: fold a slip once and drop it into the manila file; close the flap
actions.stamp: press a rubber stamp onto a card (used once, STATUS: OPEN in ch15-s09)
actions.holdUp: hold an object up into the lamp's light for the camera (a card, a slip, a graphics card), then lower it

rig.rules: the script uses only these six actions; any other gesture (turning a page, sliding a strip, tapping, inking a tag, tilting a card) is staged as a variant of pin, unpinDrop or holdUp with the same sprites; no magnifier, no coat hook, no scissors, no tweezers

notes: Not a real person and never a likeness. Kit: handArt sprites on a two-bone forearm rig (forearm + wrist) with the cuffs as separate paper layers so the rim light reads. Defined here once; every shot that says 'the hands' or 'the hands' means this rig.
